title: Freya and the Deadline
premise: Mirabel Nystrom, a private security contractor hiding in a safe house since a botched protection job she can't remember clearly, discovers the property listed online with interior photos — meaning someone knows exactly where she is and wants her found. The listing traces back to Halcyon Group, the shadowy training network that made her and erased the witnesses to 'the incident.' As dawn extraction approaches, Mirabel and her handler Freya must decide whether to run or dismantle Halcyon's evidence chain from the inside, culminating in Mirabel choosing to testify with the burned ledger rather than escape — trading her invisibility for justice, and finally sleeping through the night.
about_author: Ines Iversen is the pen name of a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for private security firms before turning to fiction. They live in coastal Norway, where the long winters are spent plotting novels about people who know too much.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Scrolling property sites at 3 a.m. — her insomnia ritual — she finds the safe house for sale, complete with photos of her own unmade bed and the wall of maps she thought was hidden. Emotional beat: cold recognition that her invisibility was always someone else's permission, not her own skill.

chapters.title: Freya's Call
chapters.summary: Freya POV. Mirabel's handler calls twenty minutes after the listing goes live — too fast to be coincidence. Freya claims Halcyon is 'managing an exposure,' but Mirabel hears the rehearsed calm. Emotional beat: the first crack of doubt in a relationship Mirabel has staked her survival on.

chapters.title: The Incident, Again
chapters.summary: Mirabel POV, fragmented flashbacks. She reconstructs what she can of the night a client died under her protection — the gaps Halcyon's 'debriefing' left in her memory. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion that her missing hours were designed, not suffered.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: Mirabel POV. A realtor arrives with strangers; Mirabel watches from a neighbor's attic as buyers photograph the safe room's reinforced door. One visitor isn't a buyer — she photographs the escape routes. Emotional beat: hunted, and realizing the hunt is professional, patient, and paid.

chapters.title: The Training Ledger
chapters.summary: Freya POV. Freya retrieves an encrypted ledger of Halcyon's contractors, clients, and 'sanitization' orders — insurance she's kept for years. She must decide whether Mirabel is a liability to erase or an ally to arm. Emotional beat: Freya's guilt, and the corrupt arithmetic she's been running.

chapters.title: Extraction at Dawn
chapters.summary: Mirabel POV. Freya offers the standard exit: a dawn flight, new name, new country, the incident permanently unexplained. Mirabel asks one question — who ordered the client's death — and Freya's silence answers it. Emotional beat: the choice crystallizes; running means living the lie forever.

chapters.title: What Halcyon Made
chapters.summary: Mirabel POV. She breaks into a defunct Halcyon training facility and finds her own file — including the sanctioned memory-suppression protocol used after the incident. Emotional beat: horror at realizing the person she's been mourning in herself was amputated on purpose.

chapters.title: The Neighbor
chapters.summary: Neighbor Dagmar's POV. An elderly woman who has watched 'the quiet tenant' for months, Dagmar saw the photographer and took her own pictures. She approaches Mirabel not with fear but with a USB stick. Emotional beat: unexpected solidarity from the civilian world Mirabel thought she'd left.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Freya POV. Halcyon flags Freya's ledger access; her own extraction is cancelled and a sanitization team assigned. She burns her cover documents and drives toward the safe house, knowing she's now prey alongside Mirabel. Emotional beat: liberation and terror arriving in the same breath.

chapters.title: First Contact
chapters.summary: Mirabel POV. The photographer from the open house corners Mirabel in a parking garage — not to kill her, but to recruit: she's a journalist holding three other Halcyon survivors' testimony. Emotional beat: the vertigo of learning she was never alone, only isolated by design.

chapters.title: The Network Map
chapters.summary: Mirabel and Freya POV alternating. Pooling the ledger, Dagmar's photos, and the journalist's files, they map Halcyon's chain: trainers, funders, the client who died, and who ordered the cover-up — Halcyon's founder, Voss. Emotional beat: the thrill of a plan replacing the paralysis of fear.

chapters.title: Safe House Siege
chapters.summary: Mirabel POV. The sanitization team hits the safe house at night. Mirabel and Freya escape through the routes in the listing photos — the exposure that threatened them becomes their survival. Emotional beat: turning the violation into a weapon, and the bond between the two women forged under fire.

chapters.title: Dagmar's Price
chapters.summary: Dagmar POV. The team, frustrated, visits Dagmar; she lies brilliantly and pays for it with a ransacked home. Mirabel finds her afterward. Emotional beat: guilt, and the theme made flesh — ordinary people paying for the powerful's secrets.

chapters.title: Voss's Office
chapters.summary: Freya POV. Freya walks into Halcyon HQ under an old credential to copy Voss's private server, buying time with the one thing he trusts: money. She gets ninety percent out before an alarm she suspects was deliberate. Emotional beat: Freya realizing Voss always knew what she was.

chapters.title: The Missing Ten Percent
chapters.summary: Mirabel POV. The missing files concern the dead client — and Mirabel's own authorization signature, forged. Voss has been holding her 'consent' as blackmail for years. Emotional beat: rage at being made complicit in her own erasure.

chapters.title: Flight Window
chapters.summary: Mirabel POV. The journalist's source inside air traffic confirms the original dawn flight still exists — Voss is using it to move the physical ledger copies out of jurisdiction. Destroy the shipment, or let it vanish forever. Emotional beat: the deadline made concrete, the noose and the exit in one.

chapters.title: Freya's Confession
chapters.summary: Freya POV. On the road, Freya admits she ran Mirabel's original debriefing — she helped build the amnesia to protect herself. Mirabel's response isn't forgiveness or fury but a cold redistribution of tasks. Emotional beat: trust broken and rebuilt on honest, uglier terms.

chapters.title: The Hangar
chapters.summary: Mirabel POV, climax part one. Infiltrating the airfield, Mirabel confronts Voss among the crates of ledgers. He offers her the one thing she wants: the memory of the incident, unredacted. Emotional beat: temptation at gunpoint — truth as a bribe.

chapters.title: What Really Happened
chapters.summary: Mirabel POV, climax part two. Voss plays the incident recording: the client was killed on Halcyon's orders, and Mirabel — drugged, half-aware — tried to stop it. She takes the drives, sets the fire, and lets Voss believe she's taking the deal. Emotional beat: grief finally with its true object, and cold, earned resolve.

chapters.title: Dawn
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The flight leaves carrying ash and decoy drives; Voss learns mid-air that the real ledger went to three newspapers and a prosecutor simultaneously. The sanitization team, suddenly evidence of a conspiracy, scatters. Emotional beat: the network burning from its own center, justice arriving not with violence but with exposure.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Mirabel POV. Months later, she gives her statement — name, face, record — in a hearing room with cameras outside. Freya watches from the gallery; Dagmar brings flowers. Emotional beat: choosing visibility as the final act of self-reclamation.

chapters.title: Freya and the Deadline
chapters.summary: Mirabel POV, epilogue. She rents a small apartment with windows on two sides and sleeps the whole night through for the first time in years — waking not to a threat but to daylight, and to a message from Freya about honest work. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace; inheritance reclaimed as a future instead of a debt.
